content: A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, you should contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, you should consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before starting dolutegravir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. If you are pregnant, notify your doctor before using this medication. Treatment with dolutegravir can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication does pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests: While taking this medication, regular laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver and kidney function tests, viral load measurements, and T-cell counts) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. For the 10-milligram tablets, keep them in their original container with the desiccant (drying agent) inside. Ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Dolutegravir is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications (such as new infections or cancer) and improves your quality of life. Dolutegravir belongs to a class of drugs known as integrase inhibitors. It is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items (such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. How to Use: Read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting dolutegravir and each time you get a refill. Take this medication at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking sucralfate or products containing aluminum or magnesium (such as antacids, laxatives, or buffered medications). If you are also taking calcium or iron supplements (including vitamins/minerals containing calcium or iron), take dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. The dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, age, and other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor. Side Effects: Headache and difficulty sleeping may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects.
